slides.headline: He was still working on mathematics at his desk the day he died.
Shreeram Shankar Abhyankar, born in Ujjain, India, died November 2, 2012, while working at Purdue University.
slides.body: He earned his PhD at Harvard under Oscar Zariski, then spent his career at Purdue, becoming the Marshall Distinguished Professor of Mathematics in 1967.

slides.headline: Abhyankar's Conjecture, Abhyankar's Lemma, and the Abhyankar-Moh Theorem - foundational work in algebraic geometry.
slides.body: He supervised 28 PhD students and received multiple honorary doctorates internationally, putting an Indian-born mathematician at the center of 20th-century algebraic geometry.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat is built partly by people whose names never trend, doing work that outlasts them.
slides.body: Abhyankar's theorems are still cited in mathematics departments worldwide - a quieter but lasting form of Indian intellectual export.
